sections.description: Skeleton of the story's ordered beats — one per eventual film section. Order = final screen order. Expanded into full prose/shots by the scene_detail pass. Since v0.3.0 (the any-length chapter architecture) this is the GLOBAL merge of every chapter's own chapter_outline sections (each chapter contributes >= 1 by its own schema floor) — minItems relaxed from 2 to 1 so a single-chapter, very-short-duration film (e.g. a bare-premise short story at the derived-duration floor) cannot fail validation merely for having one section.

id.description: Sequential: scene_1, scene_2 … MUST use this exact form (not 's01') — downstream steps parse the scene number from it.

emotion.description: The ONE feeling the audience should have during this section (e.g. 'curiosity', 'unease', 'comic relief', 'quiet dread', 'acceptance'). Authored as a coherent film-wide emotional arc BEFORE locations/events are chosen; every later stage (framing, lighting, motion, score) serves this value.

mode.description: 'dialogue' iff a character SPEAKS in this beat — the story gives them a line, direct or faithfully-converted reported speech; otherwise 'narration'. Classify honestly from the story: a dialogue-rich story correctly yields mostly dialogue sections. Carried forward unchanged by the scene_detail pass.

brief.description: One or two sentences on the strongest visual EVENT this beat depicts — name the action as the subject (e.g. 'a fist knocks on the door'), not a character standing or looking. A skeleton for the scene_detail pass to expand into a full sceneBrief — not the final shot description.

entities.description: Bible ids (characters/locations/objects) VISIBLE across this section — used by the scene_detail pass to re-inject canonical looks. List EVERY character physically present, including anyone the speaker talks to.

budgetSec.description: DETERMINISTIC, injected by plan.chapter_merge (mode:sections) — never authored by an LLM. This section's own chapter's durationSec divided evenly by that chapter's own section count. A PROPORTIONAL BUDGET, not a cap: it scales with the chapter's length and its own section count, both unbounded. The scene_detail pass reads this directly instead of computing its own T÷N estimate. Absent only if the source chapter's durationSec was itself missing/invalid (anomalous).

targetShotCount.description: DETERMINISTIC, injected alongside budgetSec: max(1, round(budgetSec / secondsPerShot)) — floored at 1 and deliberately UNBOUNDED above so it stays proportional to the section's allocated budget rather than becoming a cap (plan.chapter_merge >=0.5.1, secondsPerShot default 8). The exact number of shots the scene_detail pass should emit for this section. Absent exactly when budgetSec is absent.
